correctness.rationale: At the start of each round the adopter set is a prefix. Its only eligible nonadopter sees fraction 1/2 or 1 at the final leaf. Even a later vertex activated in that round sees the old state, so the prefix length increments by at most one. The choice of frontier is measurable before that round; its fresh coin has success probability 1/(s+2) given the entire past, independently of which vertex is selected. Extending the coin sequence past absorption gives K_t=min(m,Σ_{j=2}^{t+1}B_j). The untruncated generating function is (t+1)⁻¹∏_{l=1}^t(1+z/l), giving the stated shifted Stirling indices, with K_0=0 and no completion before m rounds. For fixed k its coefficient apart from (t+1)⁻¹ is the kth elementary symmetric function of {1/l}, asymptotic to (log t)^k/k!: the repeated-index terms in the kth power of the harmonic sum for k≥2 are O((log t)^(k−2)Σ l⁻²). Thus the highest allowed k=m−1 gives the claimed survival tail, including the exact m=1 survival 1/(t+1). The divergent sum of independent coin probabilities gives almost-sure completion; integration of the tail gives finite positive moments exactly for r<1. For the depth limit the untruncated sum has mean and variance log(t+1)+O(1), and bounded summands give Lindeberg. Inverting P(T_m≤t)=P(Σ B_j≥m) at t=floor(exp(m+x sqrt m)) gives standardized threshold −x+o(1) and limit Φ(x); tightness gives the stated law of large numbers. The frozen finite verifier was inspected, not executed, and no finite experiment is used to justify the limits.
residual_risks: Only the rooted, strict-threshold path and independent frozen synchronous rounds are verified. In particular the interior threshold fraction ceases to qualify at θ=1/2, and asynchronous updating does not preserve the same clock argument.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the exact discrete finite-round realization of a classical cycle/record law by the specified synchronous path. The closest exact inverse-age path result gives more than the fixed-depth tail: it gives a full continuous-time path law, from which the analogous log-depth Gaussian follows directly. So neither the tail exponent, the logarithmic-depth phenomenon in general, nor the Stirling law as a probability identity should be regarded as a free-standing novelty claim. The continuous formula is not the integer-round law, and the originating Monte Carlo model updates asynchronously. The originality decision rests on the exact synchronous path identification and its protocol-specific consequences.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed synchronous path formulation could already realize the same record process. The relative priority of the distinct same-day continuous record is unresolved, and the confirmed overlapping consequences are not counted as separate novelty.

value.rationale: The endpoint-seeded path is a natural minimal geometry for propagation by a single advancing frontier, and the inherited inverse-age rule gives a reason to ask about delay at each depth. The exact law predicts finite-horizon success probabilities for arbitrary depth and number of synchronous rounds, including the hard one-step-per-round cutoff; neither a large-time tail nor the continuous path law gives those probabilities. This provides a precise benchmark for a parallel aging protocol and distinguishes eventual consensus from completion on useful finite horizons. The limit statements explain the discrete clock but are not treated as intrinsically new asymptotic mechanisms.
residual_risks: The benchmark is for this protocol, not a calibrated prediction for asynchronous simulations or general social networks.
